# Radio Group

A set of radios holding one answer, with the group owning the name, the value and the focus model.

```tsx
import { RadioGroup } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `radio-group` |
| Family | inputs |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | `radio`, `state-layer` |

## Behavior

The radiogroup pattern: one tab stop, arrow keys that move and select, and a single value owned here rather than by any item. Native inputs carry the semantics; this decides which one is checked and which one is the tab stop.

Headless contract: `getRadioGroupProps` in `packages/primitives/src/radio-group.ts` — importable from `@rata/primitives` without the React wrapper or any CSS.

- **The group owns the value, not the items** — A radio's whole meaning is 'one of these'. Leaving the value on the item would let two claim to be checked, which is a state the control is supposed to make impossible.
- **Native input[type=radio] sharing one `name`** — Grouping, arrow-key behaviour and form submission all come from the platform when the name is shared. Re-implementing them on divs is how a radio group ends up not announcing how many options it has.
- **Roving tabindex is derived from the value** — The checked radio is the tab stop; a group with nothing chosen is entered at its first enabled option. Deriving it means focus and value cannot disagree, because there is no second piece of state.
- **Arrow keys select as they move, and a disabled option only takes focus** — Selecting on arrow is the radio pattern. This system's disabled controls stay focusable and announced, so a disabled radio must still be reachable — it just must not become the answer.
- **No deselect** — Unlike toggle-button-group, a radio group has no way back to nothing once answered. That is the platform's behaviour and users rely on it; a clearable set of options is a different control, and this system has toggle-button-group for it.

## Props

Extends `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "role" | "onChange" | "defaultValue">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label?` | `string` | — | Accessible name for the group — the question these radios answer. |
| `labelledBy?` | `string` | — | Id of a visible element that already names this group. |
| `value?` | `string \| null` | — | The chosen value, or null for nothing chosen yet. |
| `defaultValue?` | `string \| null` | — | Starting choice for an uncontrolled group. |
| `onValueChange?` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Called with the value the group should move to. |
| `name?` | `string` | — | Form field name shared by every radio. Defaults to a generated one. |
| `orientation?` | `ButtonGroupOrientation` | `"vertical"` | Which way the options stack, and which arrows move between them. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | — | Blocks the whole question while keeping every option focusable and readable. |
| `required?` | `boolean` | — | Marks the group as requiring an answer. |

### `label`

```ts
label?: string
```

Accessible name for the group — the question these radios answer.

**Use when**

- Always, unless `labelledBy` points at a visible heading that already asks it.

**Don't use for**

- Leaving both this and `labelledBy` unset; an unnamed radiogroup announces its options with no idea what they are options for.

**Conflicts with** `labelledBy`

**Accessibility** Becomes `aria-label` on the group.

### `labelledBy`

```ts
labelledBy?: string
```

Id of a visible element that already names this group.

**Conflicts with** `label`

### `value`

```ts
value?: string | null
```

The chosen value, or null for nothing chosen yet.

**Don't use for**

- Passing it without `onValueChange` — the group would render a choice and refuse to change it.

**Conflicts with** `defaultValue`

### `defaultValue`

```ts
defaultValue?: string | null
```

Starting choice for an uncontrolled group.

Source doc: Starting choice for an uncontrolled group. Conflicts with `value`.

**Conflicts with** `value`

### `onValueChange`

```ts

```

Called with the value the group should move to.

**Don't use for**

- Assuming it only fires on click; arrow keys select as they move, which is the pattern working correctly.

### `name`

```ts
name?: string
```

Form field name shared by every radio. Defaults to a generated one.

Source doc: Shared form field name. Defaults to a generated one.

**Use when**

- A real form post, where the name is the key the server reads.

### `orientation`

```ts
orientation?: ButtonGroupOrientation = "vertical"
```

Which way the options stack, and which arrows move between them.

**Use when**

- `vertical` for a list of options, which is the default and the readable shape for anything with more than two.

**Accessibility** Announced as `aria-orientation`. Both axes' arrow keys still move, so a user who reaches for Down in a horizontal group does not hit a dead end.

### `disabled`

```ts
disabled?: boolean
```

Blocks the whole question while keeping every option focusable and readable.

Source doc: Blocks the whole question while keeping every option focusable.

**Don't use for**

- Disabling one option; that belongs on the radio itself.

**Accessibility** Emits `aria-disabled` on each option, never the native `disabled` attribute.

```ts

```

Marks the group as requiring an answer.

**Accessibility** Emits `aria-required` on the group.

## Use cases

### Choosing one of a few

The default: a short list of mutually exclusive options.

```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Billing period" value={period} onValueChange={setPeriod}>
  <Radio value="monthly" label="Monthly" />
  <Radio value="annual" label="Annual" description="Two months free" />
</RadioGroup>
```

One tab stop for the whole group; arrows move between options and select as they go. That is the radio pattern, and it is why a radio group is not just several checkboxes.

### An option that cannot be chosen yet

One option unavailable while the rest remain answerable.

```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Shipping" value={ship} onValueChange={setShip}>
  <Radio value="standard" label="Standard" />
  <Radio value="overnight" label="Overnight" disabled description="Not available to this address" />
</RadioGroup>
```

The disabled option still takes focus, so a keyboard user discovers it exists and reads why. Arrow keys land on it without selecting it.

### Reaching for the wrong component

The options are a filter that should be clearable, or a view switch.

```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Status" value={status} onValueChange={setStatus}>
  <Radio value="open" label="Open" />
</RadioGroup>
```

Don't. A radio group cannot go back to nothing once answered — that is the platform's behaviour and users rely on it. A clearable set of options is toggle-button-group with `deselectable`; a view switch is a tab list, which this system does not have yet.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Shipping" defaultValue="standard">
        <Radio value="standard" label="Standard" />
        <Radio
          value="overnight"
          label="Overnight"
          disabled
          description="Not available to this address"
        />
      </RadioGroup>
```

## Token recipe

### vertical

The default: a readable column of options.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| gap between options | `space.stack.xs` |
| gap between group label and options | `space.stack.2xs` |
| group label color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| group label font-size | `type.label.size` |
| group label font-weight | `type.label.weight` |

### horizontal

A row, for two or three short options that fit on one line.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| gap between options | `space.gap.lg — wider than the vertical step, so two options on one line do not read as one phrase` |
| gap between group label and options | `space.stack.2xs` |
| group label color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| group label font-size | `type.label.size` |
| group label font-weight | `type.label.weight` |
